subject: Re: Continue runMCMC() with existing samples

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Continue runMCMC() with existing samples
parts:
Good question, Keith.  I'm glad to hear that you find runMCMC() easy to use.  That said, to achieve what it sounds like you're after, you would not use runMCMC().

Instead of:

samples10 <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, niter = 10)   ## generate first 10 samples
## cannot run for 10 more samples using runMCMC

You would use:

Cmcmc$run(10)   ## generate first 10 samples
samples10 <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)
## inspect first 10 samples, contained in samples10 matrix, if you wish
Cmcmc$run(10, reset = FALSE)    ## run for 10 more samples
samples20 <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)   ## extract all 20 samples

Another nuance to mention: when you execute runMCMC(), it "resets" the MCMC algorithm.  Specifically, all adaptive samplers are reset to their initial (pre-adative) state.  If you truly want to "extend an MCMC chain for more samples), then you really need to use the Cmcmc$run(..., reset = FALSE) , which prevents the MCMC from "resetting", and does in fact continue the same MCMC chain.

Cheers,
Daniel



On Wed, Mar 15, 2023 at 9:28 AM Keith Lau <genw...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi there,

I know the MCMC chain will continue from where it left off if I run runMCMC() again. I found it will not keep the existing samples. I would like to ask how I can keep the existing samples. For instance, if I first set niter = 10 and N = number of parameters, it will return 10*N. I re-run runMCMC() again, it also returns 10*N, but I want to have 20*N (including the previous samples). How can I achieve this goal by runMCMC()? I stick to  runMCMC() because it is easy to use. Thanks a lot!

Keith

messages.subject: Re: Continue runMCMC() with existing samples
parts:
Thank you, Daniel. Using Cmcmc$run(10)  and "reset" nuance is very informative. I got two further questions:

1. Does  Cmcmc$run(10) or  Cmcmc$run(10, reset = FALSE) involve adaptive sampling?

I imagine that I need to tune the MH algorithm with an adaptive algorithm for the FIRST run. For later runs, I simply need to increase the MCMC length without the adaptive MH and burn-in period.

2. How to keep the sample output format as runMCMC() when I use Cmcmc$run(10)?

In my code, I used (for the FIRST run):

samples <- runMCMC( Cmcmc , niter = 5000, nburnin = 5000, nchains= 2
                                              ,samplesAsCodaMCMC=TRUE
                                              ,samples=TRUE
                                              ,summary=TRUE
                                              ,WAIC = TRUE
                                              ,setSeed = 1)

For later runs, I wonder how can I keep to obtain the same format of the output results ("samples" here) by using Cmcmc$run(5000, reset = FALSE )?

Especially, I run multiple chains (nchains= 2 ), require  samplesAsCodaMCMC=TRUE , samples=TRUE, summary=TRUE,  WAIC = TRUE, and set random seed. If I just use Cmcmc$run(10), it is unclear to me how to obtain the same output format.

Keith

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Continue runMCMC() with existing samples
parts:
Great questions, Keith.

I suggest you read Chapter 7 (MCMC) of the NIMBLE User Manual. This will help answer many of your questions.

Briefly:

1. Both Cmcmc$run() with or without using the reset argument performs adaptive sampling.  The samplers used in nimble - those of which undergo adaptation - are always adapting, unless you disable it using the sampler control list argument "adaptive = FALSE".  The User Manual describes providing control options to samplers, when you configure the MCMC.

Also, implemented as such, you do not need to worry about the adaptation.  You can run the MCMC algorithm for as long as you want, discard whatever initial samples you'd like as burn-in, then safely use the remaining samples for inferences.

2.  Regarding the options you use for runMCMC:

samples <- runMCMC( Cmcmc , niter = 5000, nburnin = 5000, nchains= 2
                                              ,samplesAsCodaMCMC=TRUE
                                              ,samples=TRUE
                                              ,summary=TRUE
                                              ,WAIC = TRUE
                                              ,setSeed = 1)

You can accomplish the iterations and burnin using:
Cmcmc$run(10000)
Then extract all 10000 samples.
Then drop the first 5000 samples as burnin.

You can accomplish two chains by calling Cmcmc$run() again.

You can calculate the summer metrics using:
samplesSummary(samplesArray)

For WAIC, you will need to enable the WAIC calculations as:
buildMCMC(..., enableWAIC = TRUE).
Then, after running the MCMC, you can later extract the WAIC value using:
Cmcmc$getWAIC()
Note, this will give you the WAIC calculated separately for each chain (calling getWAIC after executing each chain).  If this is a major concern for you, we could describe a work-around to calculate WAIC using the samples from both chains.

For getting the samples as a coda object, use the as.mcmc() and as.mcmc.list() functions from the coda package:
coda::as.mcmc(samplesArray)

I hope this gets you started.  Keep at it.

Daniel
